questions.question: The property of rock or soil that indicates the ability of allowing fluids to flow through it is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Permeability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Permeability** is a measure of the ability of a material (such as rock or soil) to transmit fluids.
 
• It is an important property in **hydrogeology**, **soil science**, and **petroleum engineering**.
 
• Permeability is influenced by the size, shape, and connectivity of the pores in the material.
 
• Materials with high permeability, like sand and gravel, allow fluids to flow through them easily.
 
• It is typically measured in units of area, such as **Darcy (D)** or **millidarcy (mD)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Porosity:**

 
 
• Porosity refers to the volume of pores or voids in a material and is expressed as a percentage of the total volume.
 
• High porosity does not necessarily mean high permeability; it depends on the connectivity of the pores.
 
 
 
• **Hydraulic Conductivity:**
 
 
• It is a specific measure of permeability that quantifies the ease with which water can move through pore spaces or fractures.
 
• Hydraulic conductivity is typically measured in meters per second (m/s).
 
 
 
• **Capillary Action:**
 
 
• This is the ability of a liquid to flow in narrow spaces without the assistance of external forces, often against gravity.
 
• It is a critical factor in soil moisture movement and plant water uptake.
 
 
 
• **Darcy's Law:**
 
 
• A fundamental equation that describes the flow of a fluid through a porous medium.
 
• It states that the flow rate is proportional to the pressure drop and the permeability of the material.

questions.question: The core of the Great Himalayas is composed of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Granite**__.

The Great Himalayas, also known simply as the Himalayas, stretch across five countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China, and Pakistan. They form the planet’s highest mountain range and are home to some of the world's tallest peaks, including Mount Everest. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The core of the Great Himalayas, being the result of such colossal tectonic forces, is primarily composed of metamorphic and igneous rocks, due to the immense pressure and heat generated by the collision of the continental plates.

 

 
• **Granite**, an igneous rock, is found extensively in the crust of the Earth and forms a significant part of the continental crust. Granite is formed from the slow cooling of magma underground. Due to the intense tectonic activities and the melting of the crust in certain areas, granite is indeed one of the key components of the core of the Great Himalayas.

**Therefore, the core of the Great Himalaya is mainly composed of granite. Hence, option 2) granite is the correct answer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The presence of granite and other igneous and metamorphic rocks in the core of the Great Himalayas is a testament to the dynamic earth processes. 
 
• These processes are not only responsible for forming mountains but also influence climate patterns, biodiversity, and human cultures in the region.
 
• The study of the Himalayas' geology offers valuable insights into past plate tectonic movements and helps in understanding the potential for future seismic activity in this seismically active region.

questions.question: What is the rate of movement of tectonic plate boundaries?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1-2 inches per year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tectonic plates** are massive slabs of the Earth's lithosphere that fit together like a puzzle and float on the semi-fluid asthenosphere below.
 
• The **rate of movement** of tectonic plates is generally very slow, measured in terms of inches or centimeters per year.
 
• The typical movement rate of tectonic plate boundaries is approximately **1-2 inches per year**, which equates to about **2.5-5 centimeters per year.**
 
• This movement is caused by **convection currents** in the Earth's mantle, where heat causes the mantle material to flow and drag the plates along.
 
• Such movements are responsible for **earthquakes, volcanic activity, and the formation of mountain ranges** at plate boundaries.
 
• For instance, the **San Andreas Fault** in California is an example of a transform boundary where plates slide past each other at a rate of around 2 inches per year.
 
• Over millions of years, these small movements lead to **significant geological changes**, such as the drifting apart of continents, forming features like the Atlantic Ocean.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1-2 mm per year**__

 __
 
• This is an **incorrect option** because tectonic plates move at a much faster rate than this.
 
• Movements of only **1-2 mm per year** are more typical for processes like **land subsidence or soil erosion**, not tectonic plates.
 
 
 
• **1-2 meters per year**__
 __
 
• This rate is **too high** and does not correspond to the typical movement of tectonic plates.
 
• Such rapid movement is rare and might only occur during **catastrophic events like landslides or glacier flows**.
 
 
 
• **2-5 km per year**__
 
 
• This is an **unrealistic rate** for tectonic plate movement.
 
• Movements of kilometers per year are associated with **fast-moving objects** like glaciers or ocean currents, not geological plates.

questions.question: The original non-metamorphic rock that undergoes profound physical or chemical changes leading to the formation of a metamorphic rock is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protolith**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **protolith** refers to the original, pre-existing rock from which a metamorphic rock is formed due to intense heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids.
 
• The protolith can be of **igneous, sedimentary, or even earlier metamorphic origin**, depending on the geological environment.
 
• Examples of protoliths include **shale** (which can metamorphose into slate or schist), **limestone** (which transforms into marble), and basalt (which can turn into amphibolite).
 
• The transformation process involves **recrystallization, deformation, and chemical reactions**, but the rock remains solid during metamorphism.
 
• The study of protoliths is essential for understanding the **geological history** and tectonic settings of an area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metamorphic Rocks:**

 
 
• These are rocks that have undergone transformation from their original form (protolith) due to extreme pressure, temperature, or chemical processes.
 
• Common examples include **gneiss, marble, schist, slate, and quartzite**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Metamorphism:**
 
 
• **Contact Metamorphism:** Occurs when rocks are heated by nearby magma or lava.
 
• **Regional Metamorphism:** Happens over large areas due to tectonic forces causing high pressure and temperature.
 
• **Hydrothermal Metamorphism:** Involves chemical alterations caused by hot, mineral-rich fluids.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Processes:**
 
 
• **Recrystallization:** Formation of new mineral grains that are more stable under metamorphic conditions.
 
• **Foliation:** Alignment of minerals creating a layered or banded appearance, common in rocks like schist.
 
 
 
• **Regolith vs. Protolith:**
 
 
• **Regolith:** Loose, unconsolidated material covering solid rock, commonly found on Earth's surface.
 
• **Protolith:** The solid, original rock that transforms into a metamorphic rock under specific conditions.

questions.question: Nife layer of earth is situated in the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Core**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Nife layer of the Earth refers to its **inner core** and **outer core**, which are primarily composed of Nickel (Ni) and Iron (Fe).
 
• The Earth's core is divided into a solid inner core and a liquid outer core.
 
• The inner core has a radius of about 1,220 kilometers, while the outer core extends up to about 3,400 kilometers.
 
• The core is the hottest part of the Earth, with temperatures reaching up to 5,700 K (5,430 °C).
 
• The movement of the liquid outer core generates the Earth's magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earth's Layers:**

 
 
• The Earth is composed of three main layers: the crust, the mantle, and the core.
 
• The crust is the outermost layer, the mantle lies beneath the crust, and the core is the innermost layer.
 
• The mantle is made of silicate rocks that are rich in magnesium and iron.
 
 
 
• **Geological Terminology:**
 
 
• The lithosphere includes the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle.
 
• The asthenosphere is a semi-fluid layer upon which the lithosphere floats.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field:**
 
 
• The Earth's magnetic field is generated by the movement of molten iron and nickel in the outer core.
 
• This magnetic field protects the Earth from solar winds and cosmic radiation.
 
 
 
• **Plate Tectonics:**
 
 
• The movement of tectonic plates is driven by the heat from the Earth's core.
 
• This movement causes earthquakes, volcanic activity, and the formation of mountain ranges.

questions.question: The oceanic crust of the earth mainly consists of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**silica and magnesium**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Earth has three layers namely the crust, mantle and core.
 
• **Earth's crust is the earth's outermost layer and is divided into Oceanic crust and Continental crust**.
 
 
• **The crust comprises more than 90% of igneous and metamorphic rocks, and the rest with minerals, sandstones etc.**
 
 
 
• **The oceanic crust is mostly made up of basalt rocks** which are called volcanic rocks and are formed at oceanic ridges where tectonic plates are separated and is a thin and denser than the continental crust
 
 
• **This oceanic crust is referred to as "Sima" which means Silicon and Magnesium. Hence option 1 is correct.**
 
 
 
• Silica or quartz is the most abundant material on earth's crust and is an oxide of silicon (Si).
 
• Magnesium (Mg) helps major organs like the Heart, bones and Muscles function smoothly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron is one of the most abundant metals on Earth and forms its Core. As an Alloy, Iron is used in manufacturing Steel, machinery, buildings etc.**
 
• Nickel (Ni) is a silvery white metal used in plating, and Nickel alloys in turbine blades and propeller shafts etc.
 
• Alumina or Aluminium oxide is a colourless crystalline substance used in abrasion resistant tiles and cutting tools.
 
• **The continental crust, the outermost layer of the earth's lithosphere forms a continental landmass, on the earth and is formed at the subduction zones.**
 
 
• Subduction zones are the place where tectonic plates converge.

questions.question: The mohororvicic (Moho) discontinuity separates?

options.text: Earth's crust and the inner core

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earth's crust and the mantle**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mohorovičić (Moho) discontinuity is the boundary that separates the Earth's crust and the mantle.
 
• It was discovered by Andrija Mohorovičić, a Croatian seismologist, in 1909.
 
• The Moho discontinuity marks a distinct change in seismic wave velocities, indicating a change in composition between the crust and the mantle.
 
• It is located at varying depths beneath the Earth's surface, typically around 35 kilometers beneath continents and about 7-8 kilometers beneath ocean floors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Earth's crust is the outermost solid shell of the planet, composed of a great variety of igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks.
 
• The mantle lies beneath the crust and extends to a depth of about 2,900 kilometers. It is composed mainly of silicate minerals rich in magnesium and iron.
 
• Seismic waves travel faster through the mantle than through the crust due to the differences in their compositions and densities.
 
• The study of seismic waves and discontinuities like the Moho helps geologists understand the internal structure and composition of the Earth.

questions.question: Which of the following rocks are formed during rock metamorphism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Slate**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Slate** is a type of **metamorphic rock** that is formed through the metamorphism of shale.
 
• Metamorphic rocks are formed under the influence of **high pressure and temperature**, which alter the mineral composition and structure of the original rock.
 
• Other examples of metamorphic rocks include **schist, gneiss, and marble**.
 
• Metamorphism can occur due to tectonic processes such as continental collisions, which generate significant pressure and heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conglomerate** and **Sandstone** are examples of **sedimentary rocks**, which are formed from the accumulation and lithification of sediment.
 
• **Basalt** is an example of an** igneous rock**, which is formed from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.
 
• Metamorphic rocks often **exhibit foliation, a layered or banded appearance** resulting from the alignment of mineral grains under directional pressure.
 
• Metamorphism can be regional, affecting large areas of the crust, or contact, occurring adjacent to igneous intrusions where heat is a dominant factor.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of sedimentary rocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sandstone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sedimentary rocks are types of rock that are formed by the accumulation or sedimentation of minerals or organic particles at the Earth's surface, followed by cementation.
 
• Typical sedimentary rocks are sandstone, limestone, shale, Gypsum, etc. 
 
• These are also known as aqueous or stratified rocks.
 
• the rocks are well stratified and show well-defined bedding planes.
 
• The rocks are soft and can be easily split up along the bedding as well as normal planes.
 
• The properties of the sedimentary rocks vary considerably depending upon the nature of the sediment and the type of bond between the sediment and grains.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Igneous rock: 

 
 
• It is formed by heating and cooling lava or magma.
 
• It can be formed with or without crystallization.
 
• Types of igneous rock:
 
 

 
• Intrusive igneous rock: These rocks crystallize below the earth’s surface resulting in large crystals as the cooling takes place slowly. Diorite, granite, pegmatite are examples of intrusive igneous rocks.
 
• Extrusive igneous rock: These rocks erupt onto the surface resulting in small crystals as the cooling takes place quickly.

 
• The cooling rate is for a few rocks is so quick that they form an amorphous glass.
 
• Basalt, tuff, pumice are examples of extrusive igneous rock.

questions.question: Sam talks about an example of an igneous rock. Which of the following can it be?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basalt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are many different kinds of rocks which are grouped under three families on the basis of their mode of formation. They are: -
 
• Igneous Rocks - Igneous rock is formed through the cooling and solidification of magma or lava. The magma can be derived from partial melts of existing rocks in either a planet's mantle or crust.
 
 
• ​The two main categories of igneous rocks are extrusive and intrusive
 
 
• Extrusive rocks__ are formed on the surface of the Earth from lava, which is magma that has emerged from underground. example-pumice, obsidian, andesite, rhyolite, and basalt.
 
• __Intrusive rocks __are formed from magma that cools and solidifies within the crust of the planet. example-Diorite, granite, pegmatite.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Sedimentary Rocks — Sedimentary rocks are types of rock that are formed by the accumulation or deposition of mineral or organic particles at Earth's surface, followed by cementation. example-sandstone, limestone, and shale.
 
• Metamorphic Rocks —Metamorphic rocks arise from the transformation of existing rock to new types of rock, in a process called metamorphism. example- phyllite, schist, gneiss, quartzite and marble.​
